record.original_question: What is the tight worst-case number of vertex pi-floodlights needed to illuminate every simple polygon with n vertices under the same one-floodlight-per-vertex model; specifically, is the correct bound 5(n-1)/8 up to an additive constant c?

evidence.quote: It is tempting to conjecture that the correct bound for the previous conjecture is 5(n−1) 8 ± c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following illumination model for simple polygons. A vertex π-floodlight placed at a vertex v of a simple polygon P is a light source whose illuminated region is the intersection of P with a closed half-plane whose bounding line passes through v; equivalently, it is a floodlight of aperture π placed at v with a freely chosen orientation. At most one π-floodlight may be placed at each vertex of P. A set of vertex π-floodlights is said to illuminate P if the union of their illuminated regions equals P.

Let f(n) denote the smallest integer such that every simple polygon with n vertices can be illuminated by at most f(n) vertex π-floodlights under this one-floodlight-per-vertex model.

Determine the exact asymptotic value of f(n). In particular, decide whether
f(n) = 5(n−1)/8 + O(1),
i.e. whether there exists a constant c such that |f(n) − 5(n−1)/8| ≤ c for all sufficiently large n.
artifact.status_search_result: The vertex π-floodlight illumination problem remains open. Known bounds place the worst-case fraction of vertices needed between 5/8 (lower bound by Urrutia, 2002, via examples requiring 5(k+1)/(8k+9) floodlights) and 2/3 (upper bound, with refinements such as ⌊(2n−c)/3⌋ by Speckmann and Tóth where c counts convex vertices). The conjectured tight value 5(n−1)/8 ± O(1) has not been proven.

status_evidence.title: Problem 23: Vertex π-Floodlights (The Open Problems Project)
status_evidence.snippet: The fraction of n that always suffices lies between 5/8 and 2/3. Urrutia constructed examples requiring 5(k+1)/(8k+9) inward-facing floodlights, improving the lower bound factor from 0.6 to 0.625.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is listed as open with gap between 5/8 and 2/3.

status_evidence.title: Illuminating Polygons with Vertex π-Floodlights
status_evidence.snippet: Speckmann and Tóth: ⌊(2n−c)/3⌋ inward-facing edge-aligned floodlights suffice, c = number of convex vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is below 2n/3.
